title: [VSC-18] Integration and hardening: VS Code parity and plugin-reuse epic
description:
Epic-final row for epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0); decision doc docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md. Depends on every other row in the epic. The slices each proved only their own part; this row gates the whole epic.

Objective and deliverable:
1. Full regression of both plugins, in snapshots (GLOBAL rail: no in-place builds or installs). moe-vscode: `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test && npm run package`, then `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs` on the unzipped vsix's extension/bundled dir, in a snapshot whose absolute path has no UUID-shaped segment (npm 12 redacts UUIDs in `npm list` output and vsce then packages nothing; see VSC-16). moe-jetbrains: `gradlew.bat test buildPlugin --rerun` under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease, mem:gotcha-jetbrains-snapshot-gradle-test), then the onboarding smoke on the unzipped zip. Report counts against the 882a4c39 baseline (VS Code: 388 tests, 384 pass, 4 skip).
2. Cross-client corpus integrity: every moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-*.json is read by at least one Kotlin test and at least one moe-vscode test, and no corpus row carries a client-specific expectation.
3. An adversarial pass over the whole epic diff (find each row's commits with `git log --grep <task id>`; read the combined diff of moe-vscode/, moe-jetbrains/, scripts/bundle-manifest.json and .github/workflows/ci.yml): contracts that drifted between a corpus row and its consumer, duplicated helpers (a second copy of account text or of shell quoting), strict vm-harness require maps broken by a new import, listeners or terminals never disposed, notifications fired from snapshots.
4. The docs sweep held back from the slices: moe-vscode/README.md (task notifications, the Delivery section, Release Agent, the Accounts view, settings parity, worktree exclusion), moe-vscode/CHANGELOG.md (one entry for the epic), moe-vscode/MANUAL_TESTS.md (manual checks for notifications, the Accounts view and its sign-in terminal, worktree exclusion, and running the extension through VS Code Remote-WSL, which is VS Code's answer to JetBrains' "Run Agents in WSL" toggle), and the slice table in docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md (final status and landing commit per row).
5. Any cleanup a slice explicitly parked in its summary.

Not in scope: the epic's files-to-avoid (CLAUDE.md, scripts/CLAUDE.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/MCP_SERVER.md, docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, docs/roles/**, packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts, scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/postflight*, scripts/tests/worktree-*). If one of them needs a change, file a follow-up row instead.

Verification: the snapshot runs of item 1, each cited with its command, exit code and counts.
definitionOfDone: In a UUID-free git-archive snapshot of the epic's final HEAD, moe-vscode `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test && npm run package` exits 0 with counts reported against the 882a4c39 baseline, and `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs` passes on the unzipped vsix's extension/bundled dir.
Under the jetbrains-gradle lease in a snapshot, `gradlew.bat test buildPlugin --rerun` reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL with the JUnit total, and the onboarding smoke passes on the unzipped plugin zip.
Every moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-*.json is referenced by at least one test under moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin and one under moe-vscode/tests (grep listing in the summary).

moe-vscode/README.md, CHANGELOG.md and MANUAL_TESTS.md describe the epic's user-visible changes, including the Remote-WSL manual check, and the slice table in docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md shows each row's final status and landing commit.
The summary lists the adversarial findings over the whole epic diff, each fixed in this task or filed as a new row with its id.
The diff touches none of the files listed as not in scope.

implementationPlan.description:
Corpus integrity (DoD 3), read-only.

Run this from the repo root and paste its output into the summary:
for f in moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-*.json; do b=$(basename "$f"); k=$(grep -rl "$b" moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin | tr '\n' ' '); v=$(grep -rl "$b" moe-vscode/tests | tr '\n' ' '); echo "$b | kotlin: ${k:-NONE} | vscode: ${v:-NONE}"; done

Expect these corpora, each with at least one Kotlin reader and one moe-vscode reader: client-verdicts, client-delivery, client-blocker, client-settings-policy, client-accounts and client-seat-tracker. A NONE is a finding for step 3.

Then check that no row carries a client-specific expectation:
- grep -nEi 'jetbrains|vs ?code|intellij|kotlin|typescript' over the corpora, and judge every hit (a descriptive note is fine; an expectation keyed to one client is not);
- each moe-vscode consumer reads the corpus file itself, not a copied fixture;
- where the reuse decision calls for it, the consumer asserts that its labels equal moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties.

Error handling: parse each corpus with node -e inside a per-file try/catch. A corpus that does not parse is a finding, not a crash of this check.

comments.author: architect-93e0e956
comments.content:
Gap for the hardening pass (architect-93e0e956, from planning VSC-8 task-185f728f and VSC-3 task-a5f39d55). Please fix it here or file it as a row, per this row's DoD.
1. The VS Code Delivery section renders only when the task detail panel opens. VSC-8's DoD covers the initial HTML (TaskDetailPanel.getWebviewContent) and nothing else. Live updates go through postMessage 'updateTask' to media/taskDetail.js, which rebuilds only #blockerSection. So delivery evidence recorded while the panel is open (candidate, check run, receipt, attempt phase) stays stale until the panel is reopened. JetBrains refreshes its delivery section on every state update (TaskDetailDialog.refreshDeliverySection). VSC-11 edits media/taskDetail.js, which is why VSC-8 did not take the fix. A fix that avoids a second copy of the logic: have the panel post the precomputed deliveryRows (and labels) with 'updateTask', and have taskDetail.js rebuild an always-present #deliverySection from DOM text nodes, as renderBlocker does.
2. Known cross-client gap, deliberately left out of client-delivery.json. The daemon accepts any safe-integer check exitCode. JetBrains MoeJson.deliveryExitCode returns null outside the Int range (TaskDelivery.exitCode is Int), so a code such as 3221225477 shows no exit row in JetBrains, while VS Code (Number.isSafeInteger, per VSC-8's plan) renders it as failed. The risk is low: PowerShell $LASTEXITCODE and bash codes stay in range. A real fix touches MoeJson.kt and Models.kt. Serena memory decision-client-corpus-conventions has the details.

comments.author: architect-93e0e956
comments.content:
Known client divergence, filed for the epic's final pass (architect-93e0e956, from planning VSC-22 task-be543ff2). Channel auto-selection after the selected channel is deleted:
- JetBrains (VSC-22) uses ChatChannelSelection.choose: the general-type channel, else the first listed channel. Initial selection uses the same rule.
- VS Code media/chat.js updateChannels uses deselectChannel(), then selectChannels(channels[0].id): the first listed channel, with no general-type preference. Initial selection behaves the same.

The two agree whenever #general is the oldest channel. The daemon sorts snapshot channels by createdAt, and persistence.ts seeds #general first, so this is the normal case. They differ only when #general is missing or is not the oldest channel.

If exact parity is wanted: port choose() to chat.js (about 4 lines: prefer `ch.type === 'general'`, else channels[0]) and mirror ChatChannelSelectionTest cases (b) through (f). Not a corpus candidate; the rule is too small.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs takes an extracted bundle directory: <vsix>/extension/bundled for VS Code, and <zip>/moe-jetbrains for JetBrains (the CI step 'Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding' does exactly this).
- moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts prepareSandbox calls requireBundledAssets(): packages/moe-daemon and moe-proxy dist must exist and be no older than their src (mtime check), plus node_modules. node_modules/.bin is excluded from the copy, so Linux-installed node_modules should copy cleanly from a /mnt/d snapshot. That is untested, so Gate B has the Windows-npm fallback.
- `gradlew test` alone needs no dist (prepareTestSandbox).
- vsce packages nothing from a UUID path, hence /mnt/d/moe-scratch.

planningNotes.risks:
- Gate A runs three npm ci on NTFS through WSL. It is slow (minutes), so redirect output to a log outside the checkout.
- A non-epic commit landing between epic rows can break a suite. Attribute it by sha before blaming the epic.
- Docs must describe what landed: rows may be scoped down at plan time. Read completionSummaries and the code, not the slice descriptions.
- The four docs ship in the vsix (README, CHANGELOG), so any doc edit after Gate A means rerunning Gate A.
- Release the jetbrains-gradle lease even on failure. Leases are task-keyed and survive report_blocked.
- Never edit the epic's files-to-avoid; file a row instead.
